_what_this_file_is: The vocabulary of day types, and what each one is presumed to be for
allocation purposes. It is NOT a per-state rule table -- that is
2026-states.json. This file answers 'what kind of day is this?' and
states answer 'does that kind of day count here?'.
(duty days in state / total duty days) * allocable income
The denominator is the thing people get wrong. It is TOTAL duty days for
the year, not days in the season, and every state's numerator is measured
against that same denominator. So a day misclassified anywhere moves
every state's number, not just one.
Each treatment carries a status. 'settled' means the treatment is
consistent across the guidance this project has seen. 'contested' means
states genuinely differ and the per-state override in 2026-states.json
governs. 'unverified' means nobody has checked -- the engine counts the
day but flags the return as needing review, and the UI must say so.
A day type is never silently assumed.

default_denominator.definition: Total duty days from the first day of spring training through the last day of the championship season (plus any postseason duty days), as classified below.
default_denominator.note: Offseason days are excluded from both numerator and denominator. Where a state defines the period differently, it overrides here.

travel_day.label: Team travel day
travel_day.note: Widely treated as a duty day, but states differ on WHICH state a travel day is sourced to -- origin, destination, or split. Destination is used as the default because it is the commonest treatment seen; a state that says otherwise overrides it. This is a real per-state question and a genuine source of disagreement with a preparer.

off_day_in_state.label: Off day spent in a road state
off_day_in_state.note: An off day in the middle of a road trip is generally a duty day sourced to the state the player is in. Confirm per state.

spring_training.label: Spring training
spring_training.note: Spring training days are generally duty days, which is why the Arizona/Florida split matters so much: an identical player earns a different allocation depending on which league his club trains in. Whether a given state counts them, and from which date, must be confirmed per state.

injured_list_with_team.label: Injured list, travelling with the club
injured_list_with_team.note: A player on the IL is still earning salary and is generally still accruing duty days. Where he is physically present is what drives the sourcing, which is why it is a per-day question rather than a per-stint one.

injured_list_rehab.label: Rehab assignment
injured_list_rehab.note: A rehab assignment puts a player physically in a minor league city while he remains on the MLB club's payroll and IL. The correct sourcing is exactly the kind of thing that differs by state and is worth a preparer's attention. Counted, and flagged.

optional_assignment.label: Optional assignment (in the minors)
optional_assignment.note: Days on optional assignment are paid at a different rate and under a different contract. Whether they belong in the same duty-day denominator as MLB days is a question for a preparer; they are tracked separately so the allocation can be run either way.

non_team_appearance.label: Endorsement, appearance or other non-team work
non_team_appearance.note: Deliberately NOT in the team-salary duty-day count: this income is usually allocated on its own basis rather than through the team's duty-day fraction. Logged separately so it is visible to a preparer rather than lost.

allocable_income.definition: Salary and other compensation allocated across duty days.
allocable_income.note: What belongs in the allocable base -- signing bonus, performance bonuses, incentive payments, deferred money -- is treated differently by different states and is one of the questions most worth asking a preparer. This tool allocates the salary figure the player enters and says plainly what it did; it does not decide what should have been in that figure.

_note: The treatments above describe the common framework for duty-day
allocation in professional baseball. They have NOT been read off any
state's primary guidance by the author of this file.
Before this tool tells anyone a dollar figure, a preparer who does
athlete returns should review this file and the per-state table, and
each entry's status should be updated to record who checked it and
against what. Until then the UI reports day counts and allocation
percentages -- which are useful, checkable, and rate-independent --
